decisions.reason: The source defines connector and antenna placement for the later integrated board, not the separate legacy main board.
The source concerns the integrated-board layout and does not revise the separate power-board mechanical arrangement.
The integrated-board constraints do not alter the independently retained sensor-board layout.
Although both mention a battery connector, the source places J_BAT on the integrated board and does not change the separate power-board battery interface.
Grouping J_DISP_LED with the other display connectors is a mechanical-layout constraint and does not change the backlight circuit's electrical requirements.
The source does not identify the light-sensor port or change its quantity, connector type, interface, or purpose.
The source governs integrated-board connector placement and does not alter the legacy main-board connector inventory.
The new physical constraints assume the single-board architecture but do not change its consolidation or functionality-preservation requirements.
The ESP32 antenna orientation and keepout are mechanical/RF layout constraints and do not change the breakout pin-header pitch.
The placement and RF constraints do not revise the integrated board's component-sourcing or cost-optimization policy.
The source concerns connectors on the integrated board and does not change the separate sensor board's connector topology.
Battery-relative component placement does not alter the selected AXP2101 architecture, required rails, charging behavior, or efficiency goal.
